[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

AI coding agents operating without structured enterprise context generate architecturally inconsistent output: novel architecture selections instead of approved Golden Paths, security configurations from training data rather than enterprise standards, and compliance guidance that reflects general best practices rather than Gainwell-specific HIPAA, FedRAMP, and SOC 2 obligations. The result is fast generation of output that must be extensively reworked to conform to enterprise standards — negating much of the velocity benefit.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The AI Agent Context Integration Pattern defines a standardized structure for embedding Golden Path catalog references, compliance constraints, team ownership metadata, and architectural instructions into every repository as machine-readable context files. When an AI agent is invoked in any repository, it loads this context before generating any output, constraining its choices to the approved catalog and eliminating the need to re-prompt for enterprise-standard configurations.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Any repository where AI coding agents (GitHub Copilot, Claude, GPT-4o-based tools) are invoked for development assistance or autonomous generation
- Any team onboarding to the Golden Path catalog
- Any repository that is a target for intent-to-infrastructure generation
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- AI agents default to catalog-conforming implementations without additional per-session prompting
- Compliance constraints (HIPAA, FedRAMP, PHI handling) are embedded in the repository context, not in individual developer prompts
- Reduces the conformance gate failure rate for AI-generated output by providing correct context at generation time
page_texts.8:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#target-audience]

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineer**: Implementing and maintaining the `.ai/` context directory structure and Golden Path catalog integration across repositories
- **AI/ML Engineer**: Configuring AI coding agent context files to ensure catalog-conforming output for autonomous generation pipelines
- **Enterprise Architect**: Defining the compliance constraints and Golden Path references that must be embedded in repository context
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) establishes that AI agents are consumers of the Golden Path catalog, not authors of novel architecture. For this to function, AI agents must know the catalog exists, know which Golden Path applies to their current repository, know the compliance scope of the workload, and know Gainwell-specific constraints that differ from general industry practice. Without structured context integration, every AI agent session effectively starts fresh, and the developer must re-establish all enterprise context manually per session — eliminating the compound benefit of the catalog investment.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

AI coding agents consume context from multiple sources: the files currently open in the IDE, in-session user prompts, and structured context files loaded at workspace initialization. Different tools use different file conventions for agent instructions: GitHub Copilot reads `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, Cursor reads `.cursorrules`, and OpenAI Codex reads `codex.md`. Rather than maintaining separate instruction files per tool, this pattern defines a single `.ai/instructions.md` file as the canonical agent instruction source. Tool-specific bridge files, where needed, are optional thin files that reference `.ai/instructions.md` — they are not part of the required repository structure. The enterprise standard `SET_AI_CONTEXT.md` pattern (existing) establishes a human-readable context summary; this pattern extends it with machine-readable Golden Path catalog integration and compliance constraint embedding.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

AI agents using only training data and in-context code will:
- Select technology stacks based on training data popularity, not Gainwell's approved stack
- Generate Terraform using community patterns rather than Gainwell's Private Registry modules
- Generate HIPAA-scoped code without PHI-specific handling unless explicitly instructed each session
- Miss Gainwell-specific patterns (External Secrets Operator, IRSA role naming conventions, specific Kafka configuration requirements)

None of these are model failures — they are context failures. The model does not know Gainwell's choices; structured context files resolve this.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Context files must be concise enough to fit within the agent's effective context window without displacing code context
- Must support any AI agent runtime (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Code Assist, autonomous agentic frameworks) from a single source of truth, without maintaining per-tool instruction files
- Context references must link to machine-readable catalog index, not just human-readable documentation, to support autonomous pipelines
- Must be versioned alongside the repository: context files checked in and code-reviewed like any other configuration
page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Each repository contains a structured AI context directory (`.ai/`) with a set of files that collectively define the enterprise constraints, Golden Path selection, and behavioral instructions for any AI agent operating in that repository. A root-level `SET_AI_CONTEXT.md` provides the human-readable summary and references the machine-readable index. The catalog loader component in the autonomous pipeline or IDE plugin fetches the current Golden Path specification at agent invocation time, ensuring context reflects the current catalog version.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Repository Structure                                                    │
│                                                                          │
│  AGENTS.md                  ◄── Repo memory bank (cross-vendor standard) │
│                                  Read autonomously by agent at session   │
│                                  start: structure, build/test commands,  │
│                                  key conventions, do-not-touch files     │
│  .ai/                                                                    │
│  ├── context.yaml           ◄── Golden Path declaration, compliance scope│
│  ├── constraints.md         ◄── Prohibited patterns, mandatory controls  │
│  ├── instructions.md        ◄── Tool-agnostic agent instruction file     │
│  ├── catalog-ref.yaml       ◄── Machine-readable catalog index reference │
│  └── examples/              ◄── Representative conforming code snippets  │
│  SET_AI_CONTEXT.md          ◄── Human + agent readable summary           │
│  [optional tool bridges]    ◄── e.g. .github/copilot-instructions.md,    │
│                                  CLAUDE.md — thin files referencing .ai/ │
│                                                                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                 │
│  │  AI Agent (IDE or autonomous pipeline)              │                 │
│  │                                                     │                 │
│  │  0. Read AGENTS.md ────────► Repo memory bank       │                 │
│  │  1. Load .ai/context.yaml ──► Golden Path           │                 │
│  │  2. Fetch catalog spec ────► Current path template  │                 │
│  │  3. Load .ai/constraints.md ► Prohibited patterns   │                 │
│  │  4. Generate from catalog ──► Conforming output     │                 │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                 │
│                                                                          │
│  Golden Path Catalog (Platform Developer Portal)                         │
│  └── Machine-readable index ◄── Fetched at agent invocation time         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
page_texts.17:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | **Repo memory bank** — read autonomously by all major agents (GitHub Copilot cloud agent, OpenAI Codex, Claude Code) at session start. Contains repo purpose, directory structure, exact build/test/lint commands, key conventions, and files to avoid. Persistent context that applies to every agent session in the repo. See [GUID-TECH-IMPL-003](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md) for authoring guidance. | None — read natively by agent |
| `.ai/context.yaml` | Machine-readable declaration of Golden Path, compliance scope, team, and catalog version pin | Golden Path Catalog (PTN-GOV-AI-001) |
| `.ai/constraints.md` | Human and agent readable list of prohibited patterns, mandatory controls, and Gainwell-specific deviations | AI Governance Policy (PTN-GOV-AI-002) |
| `.ai/instructions.md` | Tool-agnostic agent instruction file; summarizes the active Golden Path, the three most critical constraints, and the catalog URL in plain prose that any AI agent can consume as a system/context prompt | `.ai/context.yaml`, `.ai/constraints.md` |
| `.ai/catalog-ref.yaml` | URL and authentication configuration for the catalog API endpoint used by autonomous agents | Golden Path Catalog API |
| `SET_AI_CONTEXT.md` | Human-readable summary that also serves as an agent prompt template for session initialization | All above |
| Tool-specific bridge files *(optional)* | Thin per-tool files (e.g. `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `codex.md`) that contain a single directive: load `.ai/instructions.md`. Created only if the tool does not read `.ai/instructions.md` natively. | `.ai/instructions.md` |
| Catalog Fetcher | Runtime component (autonomous pipeline or IDE plugin) that fetches the live Golden Path spec at agent invocation | Catalog API |
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Developer opens repository in IDE or autonomous pipeline initializes a generation task
2. AI agent loads `.ai/context.yaml` to determine declared Golden Path and compliance scope
3. Catalog Fetcher retrieves the current specification for the declared Golden Path from the catalog API
4. Agent loads `.ai/constraints.md` for prohibited patterns and mandatory controls
5. Agent generates output using the catalog specification as the primary template reference
6. All generated output is tagged with the Golden Path version in effect at generation time (for AI provenance, PTN-GOV-AI-005)
page_texts.19:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Monorepo**: Each service subdirectory maintains its own `.ai/` context directory, overriding root-level context for that service
- **Autonomous pipeline integration**: The context files serve as the input configuration for the intent-to-infrastructure pipeline — no separate context injection step needed
- **Multi-path repository**: Repositories hosting multiple service types declare multiple Golden Paths in `context.yaml` with service-directory mapping
page_texts.21:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- Golden Path Catalog published with machine-readable index endpoint (PTN-GOV-AI-001)
- AI Governance Policy published defining prohibited patterns and mandatory controls (PTN-GOV-AI-002)
- At least one Golden Path published for the repository's workload class
- Repository has a `service.yaml` declaring workload class (consumed by context generation tooling)
page_texts.23:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#phase-1-context-file-scaffolding]

#### Phase 1: Context File Scaffolding

1. **Create `AGENTS.md` at the repository root** — this is the first step because all major agents read it autonomously before any other context is loaded. It must cover: repository purpose, key directory structure, exact build/test/lint commands, key conventions, and files to avoid. See [GUID-TECH-IMPL-003](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md) for the mandatory sections and authoring guidance.
2. Create a cookiecutter or Copilot Workspace template that generates the `.ai/` directory structure from a `service.yaml` declaration
3. Implement `context.yaml` schema and populate it from the service's declared Golden Path and compliance scope
4. Author `constraints.md` for each Golden Path class from the Verification Contract and AI Governance Policy
5. Create the `SET_AI_CONTEXT.md` template that references the above and is usable both by humans initializing agent sessions and by autonomous pipeline catalog loaders
6. Create `.ai/instructions.md` as the tool-agnostic agent instruction file. It summarizes the active Golden Path, the three most critical constraints, and the catalog URL in plain prose. This file is the single source of truth for agent instructions across all tools.
7. *(Optional)* For teams using a tool that does not natively read `.ai/instructions.md`, create a tool-specific bridge file (e.g. `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) containing a single directive pointing to `.ai/instructions.md`. Do not duplicate instruction content in these files.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#phase-2-enterprise-rollout]

#### Phase 2: Enterprise Rollout

1. Add `.ai/` directory initialization to the Golden Path scaffold generator — all new repositories from Golden Paths include pre-populated context files
2. Update the Platform Developer Portal onboarding guide to include context file setup as step 3 of Golden Path adoption
3. Provide a migration script for existing repositories to generate context files from their `service.yaml` declaration
4. Update the AR review checklist to include context file presence and correctness
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#phase-3-autonomous-pipeline-integration]

#### Phase 3: Autonomous Pipeline Integration

1. Implement the Catalog Fetcher as a reusable component that reads `catalog-ref.yaml` and fetches the live Golden Path specification
2. Integrate the Catalog Fetcher into the intent-to-infrastructure pipeline (PTN-TEC-AI-001) as the context loading step
3. Version-pin catalog references in `context.yaml` for reproducible builds, with an explicit opt-in update process
page_texts.26:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#context-file-requirement-decision-guide]

### Context File Requirement Decision Guide

Use this guide to determine which context files are required vs. optional for a given repository type:

| Repository Type | `.ai/context.yaml` | `.ai/constraints.md` | `.ai/instructions.md` | `.ai/catalog-ref.yaml` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HIPAA-scoped microservice (GP-001) | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** (autonomous pipeline) or optional (developer-only) |
| FedRAMP-scoped microservice (GP-007) | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** |
| Shared library (no Golden Path) | Recommended | Recommended | Optional | Not applicable |
| Static frontend / docs site | Optional | Optional | Optional | Not applicable |
| Batch job (GP-002) | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** if using autonomous pipeline |
| Infrastructure-only repo (Terraform) | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** (infra generation) |

**`catalog-ref.yaml` requirement:** Required in any repository where an autonomous pipeline generates code without human session initiation. Optional (but recommended) for developer-assistance repositories.

page_texts.29:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#example-2-aiconstraintsmd]

#### Example 2: `.ai/constraints.md`

```markdown
# AI Agent Constraints — HIPAA REST Microservice on AKS

## Mandatory — Always Apply

- **PHI handling**: Never log fields declared as phi_fields in context.yaml to any output (structured or unstructured). Use the `PiiRedactionSerializer` from `com.gainwell.security.logging` for all JSON serialization.
- **Secret management**: All secrets must be injected via External Secrets Operator referencing the approved Key Vault path. Never use environment variable injection for secrets.
- **Health endpoint**: Every service MUST expose `GET /health` returning HTTP 200 with `{"status":"UP","version":"<semver>"}`.
- **OpenAPI specification**: Every service MUST include an OpenAPI 3.1 specification at `/src/main/resources/openapi.yaml`.
- **Audit events**: All PHI data access operations MUST emit an audit event to the `audit-events` Kafka topic using `AuditEventPublisher`.

## Prohibited

- Do NOT use `System.out.println` or `System.err.println` — use the structured logger only.
- Do NOT use Spring `@Value` for secrets — use External Secrets Operator.
- Do NOT use the `public` Terraform Registry — use `registry.gainwell.internal` only.
- Do NOT use Log4j 1.x or any version < 2.17.1.
- Do NOT generate self-signed TLS certificates — use cert-manager with the enterprise issuer.
```

#### Example 3: `.ai/instructions.md`

```markdown
# AI Agent Instructions — eligibility-api

This repository implements the `HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1` Golden Path.
Load `.ai/context.yaml` for the full machine-readable declaration before generating any code.

## Active Golden Path
- **ID**: HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1
- **Version**: 2026-03-01
- **Catalog**: https://platform.gainwell.internal/golden-paths/HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1

## Key Constraints (full list in `.ai/constraints.md`)
- PHI fields (`member_id`, `date_of_birth`, `eligibility_status`) must NEVER appear in log output — use `PiiRedactionSerializer`

- All code must conform to the Golden Path scaffold structure

## Stack
Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.x / Azure Kubernetes Service
```

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#example-4-aicatalog-refyaml--autonomous-pipeline-catalog-reference]

#### Example 4: `.ai/catalog-ref.yaml` — Autonomous Pipeline Catalog Reference

Used by the Catalog Fetcher in autonomous pipelines to resolve the live Golden Path specification at generation time:

```yaml
# .ai/catalog-ref.yaml
# Catalog reference for autonomous pipeline context loading.
# Updated automatically by the catalog-version-updater GitHub Action.
catalog:
  endpoint: 'https://platform.gainwell.internal/api/catalog'
  golden_path_id: 'GP-001'
  pinned_version: '1.2.0'    # Automatically updated to latest by catalog-version-updater
  auto_update: true           # false = require manual bump; true = accept automated PRs
  update_channel: 'stable'    # 'stable' | 'preview'

  # Constraints for catalog version resolution:
  min_version: '1.0.0'        # Refuse to generate against a catalog older than this
  max_version: null           # null = no upper bound

  # Fetch behavior for autonomous pipeline:
  fetch_on_pipeline_start: true
  fetch_timeout_seconds: 10
  fallback_on_fetch_failure: 'fail'  # 'fail' | 'use_pinned_version'

  # What to fetch from the catalog endpoint:
  fetch:
    - golden_path_specification  # Full path spec including scaffold structure
    - verification_contract       # All 14+ checks with expected results
    - phi_processing_guidelines   # PHI handling specific to this path version
    - approved_dependencies       # Current approved dependency list
    - prohibited_patterns         # Current prohibited pattern list
```

**Pipeline integration:**
```yaml
- name: Load enterprise context
  uses: gainwell-platform/actions/catalog-fetcher@v1
  with:
    catalog_ref: .ai/catalog-ref.yaml
    output_path: .ai/resolved-context/

- name: Generate service from intent
  uses: gainwell-platform/actions/intent-generator@v1
  with:
    intent_document: intent.yaml
    context_dir: .ai/resolved-context/
```

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Keep `constraints.md` to the most critical rules — agents with context windows full of constraints perform worse on generation quality. Curate ruthlessly.
- Version-pin the catalog reference in `context.yaml` but provide tooling for easy updates when catalog versions are released
- Review generated output against context declarations in pull request descriptions — teams should document which Golden Path version was active when AI generated a given artifact
- Create catalog-version-specific constraint files when a Golden Path version introduces breaking changes; older repositories on older versions should not receive new constraints until they migrate
page_texts.33:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Context files committed once and never updated**: The Golden Path catalog evolves. Context files must be updated when a new catalog version is released. Automate this via a scheduled PR that bumps the catalog version reference.
- **Constraints that conflict with Golden Path templates**: If a constraint prohibits something the Golden Path template itself does, the agent receives contradictory instructions. Constraints and path templates must be co-reviewed.
- **Treating context files as documentation only**: The value of context files is realized only when AI agents actually load them. Verify that the AI tooling in use actually reads the configured context files.
- **No PHI field enumeration in `context.yaml`**: For HIPAA-scoped repositories, failure to enumerate PHI fields in contextual metadata means the agent cannot apply PHI-specific constraints to those fields.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** A developer on the benefits-platform team opens GitHub Copilot in the `eligibility-api` repository and asks Copilot to generate a new REST endpoint for eligibility determination.

**Implementation:** The AI agent loads `.ai/instructions.md` and `.ai/context.yaml` at workspace initialization. The agent generates an endpoint with correct PHI redaction serialization, correct External Secrets Operator injection for the downstream API key, and a complete OpenAPI annotation — without the developer needing to specify any of these. The same behavior applies regardless of which AI tool the developer is using.

**Outcome:** Developer receives a first-draft implementation that passes the architecture fitness functions on the first commit, rather than receiving a structurally incorrect draft that requires multiple rounds of rework.
page_texts.41:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** An autonomous AI pipeline generates a new microservice from a structured intent document for the pharmacy-solutions team.

**Implementation:** The pipeline reads `.ai/context.yaml` to identify the declared Golden Path and compliance scope. It fetches the current catalog specification for `STANDARD-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1`. It loads `constraints.md` for prohibited patterns. It generates the full application + infrastructure stack using the catalog template, honoring all constraints. Generation provenance metadata (catalog version, model, timestamp) is captured per PTN-GOV-AI-005.

**Outcome:** AI-generated microservice passes both the conformance gate and fitness suite on the first pipeline run, with full provenance metadata in the evidence store.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#real-world-example-3]

### Real-World Example 3

**Context:** GP-001 is bumped to v1.3.0 with a new requirement: Prometheus metric naming convention updated from `gainwell_*` to `gw_hipaa_*`. All repositories with `.ai/context.yaml` pinned to GP-001 v1.2.0 need to be updated. Without automation, this requires manually opening PRs on 18 repositories.

**Implementation:** Platform Engineering implements a `catalog-version-updater` GitHub Action that runs on a scheduled trigger (weekly) and on GP-001 release events. The action queries GitHub for all repositories with `.ai/context.yaml` files referencing `GP-001` at a version < current. For each, it opens a PR: bumps `catalog_version` in `context.yaml`, bumps `catalog_ref` in `catalog-ref.yaml`, and includes a PR description listing the breaking changes in v1.3.0. Repository owners review and merge at their convenience.

**Outcome:** 14 of 18 repositories are updated within 1 sprint via automated PRs. 4 remain on v1.2.0 with open PRs; their teams are using the transition period to remediate the metric naming change in their services before updating the AI context.

#### Scenario 3: Autonomous Pipeline Failing Without PHI Field Declaration

The intent-to-infrastructure pipeline for the benefits-platform team generates a new `ClaimStatusService`. The pipeline reads `.ai/context.yaml` and discovers that `phi_fields` is empty. The pipeline halts at context validation: `CONTEXT-VALIDATION-001 FAIL: phi_fields must be declared for HIPAA-scoped service. Review service data model and declare all PHI field names before retrying.` The team realizes they copied the context file from a non-PHI service. They update `phi_fields` with `[claim_id, member_id, service_date, diagnosis_code]` and re-trigger the pipeline. Generation proceeds and produces correct PHI redaction wrappers for all 4 declared fields.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

- **AI context per session**: Developers re-establish Gainwell-specific context in each AI session through manual prompts; context depth and accuracy varies by developer; new developers miss compliance-critical constraints entirely
- **Generation quality**: AI-generated code fails conformance gates and fitness functions requiring 3–5 rounds of rework before passing; velocity gains eroded by correction cycles
- **Autonomous pipelines**: No structured mechanism for autonomous pipelines to know the correct Golden Path, PHI field declarations, or prohibited patterns; pipelines require human input per generation event
- **Catalog updates**: When a Golden Path version is released, there is no automated mechanism to notify AI agents operating in affected repositories; agents continue generating against obsolete specifications
page_texts.49:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

- **AI context per session**: Context is loaded automatically from repository files at every session and pipeline invocation; developers and pipelines operate against identical, current context without manual prompting
- **Generation quality**: First-pass conformance gate failure rate for AI-generated output drops 60–70% as agents generate to the correct Golden Path specification; rework cycles reduced from 3–5 to 1 or fewer
- **Autonomous pipelines**: The Catalog Fetcher reads `catalog-ref.yaml` and fetches the live Golden Path specification at generation time; pipelines generate architecturally consistent output without human context input
- **Catalog updates**: Automated weekly PRs notify teams of new catalog versions via context file updates; AI agents in all repositories are coordinated to current specifications within 1 sprint of a catalog release

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-002-ai-agent-context-integration-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** AI agents operating without structured enterprise context generate architecturally inconsistent output that fails conformance checks and requires extensive rework.

**Solution:** Standardized `.ai/` context directory in every repository that provides AI agents with the declared Golden Path, compliance scope, PHI field declarations, and prohibited-pattern constraints — loaded automatically at agent invocation.

**When to Use:**
- Any repository where AI agents are invoked for development assistance or autonomous generation
- Any repository that is a target for intent-to-infrastructure generation

**Key Benefits:**
- AI agents default to catalog-conforming implementations without manual per-session prompting
- Compliance constraints embedded in repository, not in individual prompts
- Reduces conformance gate failure rate for AI-generated output

**Implementation Complexity:** Low-Medium

**Prerequisites:** Golden Path Catalog (PTN-GOV-AI-001), AI Governance Policy (PTN-GOV-AI-002), at least one published Golden Path for the workload class

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-001, PTN-GOV-AI-002, PTN-GOV-AI-005, PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-TEC-AI-001
